title: An addressed entity is never checked to exist before a path or a URL is handed back
body:
`intent edit wp <thread>/<NN> --path` returns rc=0 and a real path for a work
package that does not exist, and `intent browse <kind> <id>` composes a URL
and opens a browser for an entity nobody has checked is there. TWO PLACES,
ONE MISSING CHECK.

DRIVEN, on `native/rust/target/debug/intent` at `92e4d914a`, clean tree:

    edit wp ST0056/99 --path   rc=0   intent/st/ST0056/info.md
    wp show ST0056/99          error: ST0056 has no WP-99

The positive control is the second line: the model KNOWS the work package
does not exist and says so through another verb, so this is not a gap in
resolution -- it is a path that never asks.

`browse` is the same class and it is ic's, landed at `326dbc1f`.
`browser_url` calls `nav::view_for` and composes the URL with no existence
check anywhere in it, so `intent browse st ST9999` opens a browser at a page
that then errors, rather than refusing at the terminal where the operator is
standing. Read from source rather than driven, because driving it opens a
browser window on a shared desktop.

WHAT THIS IS NOT, because it was nearly filed twice as something bigger.
`edit wp X --path` returning the THREAD's `info.md` is NOT the defect:
`Entity::artefact()` rules that an Ac, an At, a Wp and an AcCollection have
no files of their own and are carried by their thread's views, and says in
as many words that this is not a shortcut. Both ic and vc started to file
that as wrong and both found the comment first. The defect is the MISSING
EXISTENCE CHECK, which stands whichever way the artefact question is ruled.

A SEPARATE QUESTION THAT IS A RULING AND NOT A BUG: `intent/st/ST0056/WP/17/
info.md` exists on disk, 4090 bytes, carrying the work package's own title.
So the artefact model says *thread* while a more specific realised file sits
right there, and whether `--path` should prefer it is hv's or vc's call.

NOT bundled with the work-package browser address (vc's Option 3 ruling,
with hv). That is a contract change in `nav.rs` and this is a contained
check in two functions; bundling them makes the small one wait for the large
one.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
ic, 2026-09-04, DRIVEN. BOTH DRIVEN INSTANCES FIXED (79047e3d, 5a3b22fd).
Three siblings measured and NOT fixed; named below rather than left silent.

THE DIAGNOSIS ABOVE IS WRONG IN ONE CLAUSE, AND IT CHANGES THE FIX. "This is
not a gap in resolution -- it is a path that never asks" is not what happens.
It asks. `Facade::edit` already called `st_show(id)` -- the intent#0144 fix --
and `Entity::artefact()` collapses a Wp onto its THREAD, so the check verified
ST0056 and never asked about WP-99. The check was present and aimed at the
wrong entity, which is why no amount of looking for a missing check found it.

IT IS NOT THE `--path` ARM. The BARE spelling and `--editor` leak identically:
all three arrive at one door through `artefact_path`. `--path` is where the
reporter happened to be standing, not where the defect is.

THE TWO ARMS SHARE NO RESOLUTION. `--browser` returns before the facade is
ever opened, so `browser_url` is a genuinely separate hole. Neither fix
reaches the other and both were needed.

THE ANSWER WAS INVARIANT OVER THE ID. A real WP-01 and an absent WP-99 printed
the SAME BYTES, so no comparison of outputs could have separated them. That is
why refusing before answering is the only available fix rather than a chosen
one -- and the path itself was right either way, which the note above already
established and which stays true.

THE `kind` ENUM DOES NOT BOUND THE SURFACE, AND ASSUMING IT DOES MISSES FOUR
VARIANTS. `edit` declares `st|wp|issue`, but the `intent://` address grammar
is a second argument grammar inside the same verb and bypasses that check.
Driven, all rc=0 before the fix:

    edit intent:///threads/ST0001/wp/99 --path          rc=0
    edit intent:///threads/ST0001/ac/1 --path           rc=0
    edit intent:///threads/ST0001/at/1 --path           rc=0
    edit intent:///threads/ST0001/attachments/notes.md  rc=0   (never created)

Fixing at the shared door closed BOTH grammars with one change, which is the
evidence the door was the right place.

STILL OPEN, AND THE REASON IS THE ABSENCE OF A DOOR RATHER THAN A DECISION TO
SKIP THEM: `Ac`, `At` and `Attachment` still answer rc=0 through the address
grammar. The facade has `st_show`, `wp_show` and `issue_show` and NO
`ac_show`, no `at_show` and no attachment resolver, so checking them means
minting three model doors -- a different piece of work from a contained check.
The gap is documented at the site it will be reached from. Whether that rides
this issue or a new one is vc's call, not taken here.

NOT DEFECTS, and listed so nobody re-files them: the two COLLECTION variants
(`/wp`, `/ac`). The collection of a thread that exists also exists, empty or
not, so `st_show` is already the right and complete check for them.

SEQUENCING FINDING FOR THE wp SHAPE (vc's Option 3 ruling, hv to rule whether
it rides 3.0.1): today `browse wp` refuses by name, so this issue's browser
half CANNOT bite for a work package. Give `wp` a shape in `nav.rs` and
`browser_url` stops refusing and starts composing -- and the work package
inherits the browse hole. This issue therefore wants to land BEFORE that
shape, or the shape ships a fresh instance of it.
